evidence.title: Warton, Lancaster
evidence.text: Warton is a village, civil parish and electoral ward in the City of Lancaster in north Lancashire in the north-west of England, close to the boundary with Cumbria, with a population of around 2,000, measured at the 2011 Census to be 2,360.

evidence.title: Warton, Lancaster
evidence.text: It is a village steeped in history; its earliest recording as a settlement is made in Domesday Book written in 1086.

evidence.title: Warton, Lancaster

evidence.title: Warton, Lancaster
evidence.text: It has connections to the first President of the United States, George Washington: Washington's ancestor of seven generations, Lawrence Washington, is rumoured to have helped build the village church of St Oswald.

evidence.title: Warton, Lancaster

evidence.title: Warton, Lancaster

evidence.title: Orleans, Ontario
evidence.text: Orléans ( ; French: ] ) (officially Orléans), is a suburb of Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

evidence.title: Orleans, Ontario
evidence.text: It is located in the eastern part of the city along the Ottawa River, about 16 km from downtown Ottawa.

evidence.title: Orleans, Ontario
evidence.text: The Canada 2011 Census determined that Orléans' population was 107,823.

evidence.title: Orleans, Ontario
evidence.text: Prior to being amalgamated into Ottawa in 2001, the community of Orléans was spread over two municipal jurisdictions, the eastern portion being in the pre-amalgamation City of Cumberland, the western portion in the City of Gloucester.

evidence.title: Orleans, Ontario
evidence.text: According to the 2011 census, 62,888 people lived in the Cumberland portion of Orléans, while 44,935 people lived in the Gloucester portion.

evidence.title: Orleans, Ontario
evidence.text: Today, Orléans spans the municipal wards of Orléans, Innes and Cumberland.

evidence.title: Orleans, Ontario
evidence.text: Orléans is one of 3 areas of the post-amalgamated City of Ottawa to contain a significant francophone population, hence the community's name.
